messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High tail-latency detected for streaming websocket path /v1/stream across prod-us-west-2. p95 -> 1.8s (+600ms), p99 -> 6.4s (+4s). Errors: increased 502s on proxy, client disconnect spikes. Paging olivia (oncall).

olivia (oncall): acked. I'm joining. putting channel in high-priority. who is on runtime? :wave:

mike: i'm here, looking at proxy metrics + socket counts. tcp_close rate up on nginx-streamer.

olivia (oncall): what are customer-facing symptoms? support_anna?

support_anna: multiple customers reporting websocket stalls where no chunks arrive for 20-30s then resume. one customer (paul) posted a trace showing heartbeat gap.

paul (customer): here's their snippet (redacted):
```
[socket] last_recv=2026-03-15T10:22:03Z, next_recv=2026-03-15T10:22:34Z, missed_heartbeat=3
client: no data for 31s, connection idle, reconnected
```

ingrid (eng-runtime): curious — our runtime heartbeat is every 15s. logs show runtime sending, but proxy flush maybe stalling due to buffer pressure. grabbing logs from proxy pods.

mike: nginx stream logs show repeated "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)" and "writev() failed (32: Broken pipe)" around the same windows. Also observed a rise in socket backlog on worker nodes.

olivia (oncall): initial hypothesis: client backpressure + proxy write buffer + keepalive mismatch causing fragmentation and delayed chunk flush. Could be p99 tail due to some clients reading slowly and blocking proxies, holding file descriptors.

ingrid (eng-runtime): rolling quick check: runtime KV cache and chunking pipeline show normal latencies. no CPU spikes. only network/socket waits. grabbing strace on one streamer process.

mike: i'm going to take one nginx-streamer pod out of LB and enable debug logging. performing: 
```
kubectl -n streaming exec -it deploy/nginx-streamer -- nginx -s reopen
kubectl -n streaming annotate svc/stream-proxy critical-debug=true --overwrite
```

olivia (oncall): please also check kernel socket backlog, somaxconn, tcp_max_syn_backlog on the nodes. if FD exhaustion, we need immediate mitigation.

mike: node sysctl: somaxconn=4096, net.core.somaxconn=4096, tcp_max_syn_backlog=2048. fd count on busy nodes at ~85% of ulimit. I see a small leak of connections in CLOSE_WAIT.

ingrid (eng-runtime): runtime traces show we sometimes coalesce large frames when client window is small. runtime waits on poll() for socket until buffer drains. if proxy holds write due to slow consumer, it backs up. suggests head-of-line blocking.

olivia (oncall): mitigations we can do now: 1) route heavy clients to fallback pool (lower concurrency), 2) temporarily increase proxy write timeout and keepalive to reduce reopen churn, 3) enable aggressive chunk flush on proxy to avoid large buffered frames. choose 1/2/3.

mike: doing 2 + 3 now. applying nginx config: set proxy_send_timeout=180s -> 30s? hmm we want fewer connection closes so bump to 180s and set chunked_transfer_encoding on and sendfile off. patch: 
```
# /etc/nginx/conf.d/stream-proxy.conf
proxy_send_timeout 180s;
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```
reloading.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: deploy triggered by mike: nginx-streamer/rollout 1->2 (patch).

olivia (oncall): rolling change to 20% of pods first. watching p95/p99.

(2m pass)

mike: small improvement p95 -120ms, p99 -1.1s. still some p99 spikes. 502s reduced by ~40%.

ingrid (eng-runtime): adding a runtime patch to send smaller periodic noop frames every 5s when client hasn't read — reduce burst flush. staging patch applied to one canary pool.

olivia (oncall): can we also short-circuit requests from clients that advertise very small windows (super slow consumers)? maybe apply connection-level rate limiting on proxy.

mike: applying limit_conn/limit_rate for suspicious routes (temp): 
```
limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=addr:10m;
limit_conn addr 20;
limit_rate_after 1m;
limit_rate 128k;
```

(5m)

mike: after limits + chunked flush, p99 improved another ~600ms. tail events still present but rare.

support_anna: reaching out to impacted customers with status update: "We observed intermittent websocket stalls affecting streaming deliveries. We applied routing and proxy mitigations; we're monitoring. We'll follow up with postmortem and timeline."

paul (customer): thanks — they said stalls look better now, reconnects less frequent.

olivia (oncall): OK we have a stable mitigation but root cause unclear — likely compositional: slow consumer backpressure + proxy buffering + occasional FD leaks on nodes leading to head-of-line congestion. Need postmortem and permanent fixes.

ingrid (eng-runtime): immediate action items from runtime side: 1) land noop-heartbeat every 5s for slow consumers (reduce chunk coalescing), 2) add instrumentation for per-connection write queue time, 3) add eviction policy for hung connections >60s without progress.

mike: infra action items: 1) audit nginx-streamer buffer configs across regions, 2) add backpressure metrics to dashboards (socket write queue depth), 3) audit kernel FD/close_wait leak sources, 4) tune ulimits & autoscale thresholds to avoid fd saturation.

olivia (oncall): i'm creating incident ticket and assigning owners. incident -> INC-2026-0315-WS-TAIL. filing timeline and attaching logs.

ops-bot: :page_facing_up: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-WS-TAIL (owner: olivia).

olivia (oncall): handoff to daytime oncall in 30m. jamie (sre_lead) — can you take postmortem lead tomorrow and coordinate customers?

sre_lead_jamie: on it. will schedule postmortem meeting, want the following pre-reads: thread logs, proxy config diffs, per-conn write latency graphs, and customer traces.

ingrid (eng-runtime): i'll upload canary runtime logs and the noop-heartbeat patch PR link to the incident.

support_anna: created customer-facing summary doc and SF case updates. noting affected customers list.

olivia (oncall): final note before handoff: system stable, p99 down to baseline +200-300ms, no active escalations. continue monitoring for next 2h. handoff in 5. :thumbsup:

(5m later)

olivia (oncall): handing off to jamie for daytime. all oncall history in INC-2026-0315-WS-TAIL. closing page. :white_flag:

sre_lead_jamie: acked. will pick up follow-ups. please add action-item owners in the incident ticket.

ops-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: Reminder: create postmortem within 48h.
